mechanism_narrative: The level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is always negatively correlated with S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as high interest rates compress equity valuations and increase the cost of capital.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the time when FEDFUNDS is above 4.5%, or the Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 5.0% signals restrictive monetary policy that reduces corporate earnings growth expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 5.0%, the 20-day forward returns are positive, or the Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in residential investment (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) signals weakening demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction condition (HOUST < 1750 and RSAFS < 360000) is met in more than 50% of instances where 20-day forward returns are positive, or the Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 4.5%), the S&P 500 is expected to have negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and corporate profitability.
failure_condition: In more than 50% of the time when UNRATE > 4.5%, the 20-day forward returns are positive, or the Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The level of the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is always negatively correlated with S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as high unemployment signals weak economic conditions and reduced corporate profitability.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the time when UNRATE is above 4.0%, or the Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST below 1750) signals weakening housing market conditions and reduced consumer confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In more than 50% of the time when HOUST < 1750, the 20-day forward returns are positive, or the Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO below 110) and high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 5.0%) signals a contractionary economic environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction condition (INDPRO < 110 and FEDFUNDS > 5.0%) is met in more than 50% of instances where 60-day forward returns are positive, or the Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply contraction regime (INDPRO < 110), the S&P 500 is expected to have negative forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to reduced economic activity and lower corporate earnings.
failure_condition: In more than 50% of the time when INDPRO < 110, the 5-day forward returns are positive, or the Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.
